### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch

### Module(s)

mini.pick

### Neovim version

0.11.x

### Description

Hello, I have a small issue with the **Pick** module, and I'm not sure if I'm doing something wrong. Basically, I want to use `Pick buf_lines scope="current"` to search for specific lines in the current buffer. Specifically, I want to find all lines that start with 'j' followed by a space. Trying with `"^j "` doesn't work because the line is interpreted as starting with the line number, so the `^` modifier seems less useful in this case. Am I doing something wrong? Is there a way to remove line numbers from the picker's selection window? I know I can use a search or `vimgrep` to get the same result, but using `buf_lines` mode is simpler and faster. Thank you very much for your help.

### Reproduction

1. Create separate 'nvim-repro' config directory:
    - '~/.config/nvim-repro/' on Unix
    - '~/AppData/Local/nvim-repro/' on Windows

2. Inside 'nvim-repro' directory create a file named 'init.lua'.
   Populate it with the following content:

    ```lua
    -- Clone latest 'mini.nvim' (requires Git CLI installed)
    vim.cmd('echo "Installing `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
    local mini_path = vim.fn.stdpath('data') .. '/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim'
    local clone_cmd = { 'git', 'clone', '--depth=1', 'https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim', mini_path }
    vim.fn.system(clone_cmd)
    vim.cmd('echo "`mini.nvim` is installed" | redraw')

    -- Make sure 'mini.nvim' is available
    vim.cmd('packadd mini.nvim')
    require('mini.deps').setup()

    -- Add extra setup steps needed to reproduce the behavior
    -- Use `MiniDeps.add('user/repo')` to install another plugin from GitHub
    ```

3. Run `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-repro nvim` (i.e. execute `nvim` with `NVIM_APPNAME` environment variable set to "nvim-repro").
   Wait for all dependencies to install.

4. Replace this with description of interactive reproduction steps along with the behavior you observe.
   Feel free to include images/videos/etc, this helps a lot.

<details><summary>What to do after reporting an issue</summary>

After reporting the issue, it is safe (and even recommended for cleaner possible future bug reports) to remove 'nvim-repro' config from the system:
- Delete config directory ('~/.config/nvim-repro' on Unix).
- Delete data directory ('~/.local/share/nvim-repro' on Unix).
- Delete state directory ('~/.local/state/nvim-repro' on Unix).

</details>

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the issue!

There is no issue on the usage side. The `buf_lines` picker does compute its items as buffer lines *but* prepended with line number. This was a compromise between showing line numbers of matched lines and complexity of implementation. One of the downsides (if not the only) is that `^` indeed does not match based on actual buffer content.

I'll think about the best approach to resolve this. There are at least the following possibilities (each with its pros and cons):
- Add local option to `buf_lines` to skip prepending with line numbers. The simplest to add, but I think it is a worse user experience to not see line numbers. Not sure by how much, though.
- Implement custom `show` to show line numbers. Either as actual text in stritem or via inline extmarks (requires Neovim>=0.10). Somewhat complex solution.
- Add custom mapping to toggle showing line numbers.

If I were to follow

> Implement custom show to show line numbers. Either as actual text in stritem or via inline extmarks (requires Neovim>=0.10). Somewhat complex solution.

`buf_name` would still be part of `stritem` when `scope=all`, right? That would mean that `^` would work on the buffer content only when `scope=current`

> If I were to follow
> 
> > Implement custom show to show line numbers. Either as actual text in stritem or via inline extmarks (requires Neovim>=0.10). Somewhat complex solution.
> 
> `buf_name` would still be part of `stritem` when `scope=all`, right? That would mean that `^` would work on the buffer content only when `scope=current`

The idea is to have any "information prefix" be implemented as inline extmark. Be it only line number or buffer name plus line number. With Neovim>=0.10 as the supported version range, this is now doable, but the complexity *might* be rather high. Not sure if it will be worth it until I see the solution.

Another approach I had in mind was to use 'statuscolumn', but not sure how feasible it will be. Especially given high amount of optimizations for 'statuscolumn' rendering (like autocomputing and forcing fixed width) and ensuring proper highlighting.

What do you think of the following? ```diff diff --git a/lua/mini/extra.lua b/lua/mini/extra.lua index 8dad3db..76efd01 100644 --- a/lua/mini/extra.lua +++ b/lua/mini/extra.lua @@ -352,20 +352,31 @@ MiniExtra.pickers.buf_lines = function(local_opts, opts) for _, buf_id in ipairs(buffers) do if not poke_picker() then return end H.buf_ensure_loaded(buf_id) - local buf_name = H.buf_get_name(buf_id) or '' - local n_digits = math.floor(math.log10(vim.api.nvim_buf_line_count(buf_id))) + 1 - local format_pattern = '%s%' .. n_digits .. 'd\0%s' for lnum, l in ipairs(vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(buf_id, 0, -1, false)) do - local prefix = is_scope_all and (buf_name .. '\0') or '' - table.insert(items, { text = format_pattern:format(prefix, lnum, l), bufnr = buf_id, lnum = lnum }) + table.insert(items, { text = l, bufnr = buf_id, lnum = lnum }) end end pick.set_picker_items(items) end local items = vim.schedule_wrap(coroutine.wrap(f)) - local show = H.pick_get_config().source.show - if is_scope_all and show == nil then show = H.show_with_icons end + -- TODO: show icons when `is_scope_all` + local show = function(buf_id, items_to_show, query) + pick.default_show(buf_id, items_to_show, query) + + H.pick_clear_namespace(buf_id, H.ns_id.pickers) + for i, item in ipairs(items_to_show) do + local n_digits = math.floor(math.log10(vim.api.nvim_buf_line_count(buf_id))) + 1 + local format_pattern = '%s%' .. n_digits .. 'd│' + + local buf_name = H.buf_get_name(item.bufnr) or '' + local prefix = is_scope_all and (buf_name .. '│') or '' + + local extmark_opts = + { virt_text = { { format_pattern:format(prefix, item.lnum), 'NormalFloat' } }, virt_text_pos = 'inline' } + vim.api.nvim_buf_set_extmark(buf_id, H.ns_id.pickers, i - 1, 0, extmark_opts) + end + end local match_opts = { preserve_order = local_opts.preserve_order } local match = function(stritems, inds, query) pick.default_match(stritems, inds, query, match_opts) end local default_source = { name = string.format('Buffer lines (%s)', scope), show = show, match = match } ``` `scope=current` `scope=all`

> What do you think of the following?

This looks more or less fine, although leaving a `TODO` for one thing that worries me here is kind of not fair :) Will icon highlighting work properly with custom `MiniPickNormal` (which should be used instead of `NormalFloat`, by the way)? It also should work properly with `MiniPick.config.options.content_from_bottom = true` (although hopefully should work right away without extra changes, if I remember correctly).

And I still think both other suggestions from [this comment](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/issues/1921#issuecomment-3149581980) are valid.

Maybe there is also a fourth way of implementing custom `match`? If query starts with `^`, match against line, otherwise - full stritem. Always matching against the line is also doable, but seems like not the best for `scope='all'` case, though.

The code did become more verbose adding the icon handling, it looks like this now ```diff diff --git a/lua/mini/extra.lua b/lua/mini/extra.lua index 8dad3db..6f44384 100644 --- a/lua/mini/extra.lua +++ b/lua/mini/extra.lua @@ -352,20 +352,54 @@ MiniExtra.pickers.buf_lines = function(local_opts, opts) for _, buf_id in ipairs(buffers) do if not poke_picker() then return end H.buf_ensure_loaded(buf_id) - local buf_name = H.buf_get_name(buf_id) or '' - local n_digits = math.floor(math.log10(vim.api.nvim_buf_line_count(buf_id))) + 1 - local format_pattern = '%s%' .. n_digits .. 'd\0%s' for lnum, l in ipairs(vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(buf_id, 0, -1, false)) do - local prefix = is_scope_all and (buf_name .. '\0') or '' - table.insert(items, { text = format_pattern:format(prefix, lnum, l), bufnr = buf_id, lnum = lnum }) + table.insert(items, { text = l, bufnr = buf_id, lnum = lnum }) end end pick.set_picker_items(items) end local items = vim.schedule_wrap(coroutine.wrap(f)) - local show = H.pick_get_config().source.show - if is_scope_all and show == nil then show = H.show_with_icons end + local show = function(buf_id, items_to_show, query) + pick.default_show(buf_id, items_to_show, query) + + local icons = { directory = ' ', file = ' ' } + H.pick_clear_namespace(buf_id, H.ns_id.pickers) + for i, item in ipairs(items_to_show) do + local n_digits = math.floor(math.log10(vim.api.nvim_buf_line_count(item.bufnr))) + 1 + local format_pattern = '%s%' .. n_digits .. 'd│' + + local buf_name = H.buf_get_name(item.bufnr) or '' + local prefix = is_scope_all and (buf_name .. '│') or '' + + local path = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_name(item.bufnr) + local fs_type = vim.fn.isdirectory(path) == 1 and 'directory' or 'file' + + local virt_text = { { format_pattern:format(prefix, item.lnum), 'MiniPickNormal' } } + + local add_icon = function() + if _G.MiniIcons ~= nil then + local icon, hl = _G.MiniIcons.get(fs_type, path) + return table.insert(virt_text, 1, { icon .. ' ', hl }) + end + + if fs_type == 'directory' then + return table.insert(virt_text, 1, { icons.directory, 'MiniPickIconDirectory' }) + end + local has_devicons, devicons = pcall(require, 'nvim-web-devicons') + if not has_devicons then return table.insert({ virt_text, 1, { icons.file, 'MiniPickIconFile' } }) end + + local icon, hl = devicons.get_icon(vim.fn.fnamemodify(path, ':t'), nil, { default = false }) + icon = type(icon) == 'string' and (icon .. ' ') or icons.file + table.insert(virt_text, 1, { icon, hl or 'MiniPickIconFile' }) + end + if is_scope_all then add_icon() end + + local extmark_opts = { virt_text = virt_text, virt_text_pos = 'inline' } + vim.api.nvim_buf_set_extmark(buf_id, H.ns_id.pickers, i - 1, 0, extmark_opts) + end + end local match_opts = { preserve_order = local_opts.preserve_order } local match = function(stritems, inds, query) pick.default_match(stritems, inds, query, match_opts) end local default_source = { name = string.format('Buffer lines (%s)', scope), show = show, match = match } ``` I also liked the option of using a custom `match`, the code for it is more concise (since there's no need to reimplement the `show` logic) ```diff diff --git a/lua/mini/extra.lua b/lua/mini/extra.lua index 8dad3db..1a5d41e 100644 --- a/lua/mini/extra.lua +++ b/lua/mini/extra.lua @@ -367,7 +367,15 @@ MiniExtra.pickers.buf_lines = function(local_opts, opts) local show = H.pick_get_config().source.show if is_scope_all and show == nil then show = H.show_with_icons end local match_opts = { preserve_order = local_opts.preserve_order } - local match = function(stritems, inds, query) pick.default_match(stritems, inds, query, match_opts) end + local match = function(stritems, inds, query) + if query[1] and vim.startswith(query[1], '^') then + stritems = vim.tbl_map(function(i) + local parts = vim.split(i, '%z', {}) + return parts[#parts] + end, stritems) + end + pick.default_match(stritems, inds, query, match_opts) + end local default_source = { name = string.format('Buffer lines (%s)', scope), show = show, match = match } return H.pick_start(items, { source = default_source }, opts) end ```

> The code did become more verbose adding the icon handling, it looks like this now

Yeah, not immediately a fan of adding this just for `buf_lines`. If that could be generalized for more pickers (like `diagnostics`, perhaps), then maybe. But the diff will be even larger.

> I also liked the option of using a custom `match`, the code for it is more concise (since there's no need to reimplement the `show` logic)

Yeah, this is simpler, but unfortunately there is a need for a custom `show`. Since the matched characters are not highlighted properly.

---

Still not sure yet, but this helped. Thanks!
